rows.proof: `CAPITAL PROJECT FUNDS FY 2015`, PDF page 34 of the FY2015 annual town report. THE PAGE IS MIRRORED AND ROTATED IN ITS OWN TEXT LAYER, exactly as FY2014 page 34 is: the words read backwards (`SDNUF TCEJORP LATIPAC`) and what scans as a row at constant `top` is a COLUMN of the table, so every word is reversed, the word ORDER within a label is reversed too, and the table is transposed before anything is read. No image is involved. THE ROW GRID IS MEASURED, NOT GUESSED: adjacent projects sit 8pt apart in x and one pair is 1pt apart, so clustering on x gaps merged two projects into one. The 45 words of the APPROPRIATED FORWARD column (top 285-295) are used as the anchors instead -- one per project -- and every other word is filed to the nearest anchor centre within 4.5pt. 46 words are left over and all 46 are accounted for: the four printed column headings, the four `FYnn Capital Program` group headings with their article and town-meeting references, and the three-line footer legend. THREE MONEY COLUMNS, NAMED FROM THE PRINTED HEADER: APPROPRIATED FORWARD, EXPENDED/ENCUMBERED/TRANSFERRED, BALANCE. A narrow flag column carries `fwd`. WHAT CLOSES, ALL TO THE CENT: every project returns appropriated/forward less what was expended, encumbered or transferred as its balance -- 43 of 44 state all three and the 44th (`08/02 ATM Development of Cemeteries`) prints no expended figure at all, so nothing asserts it there; and all THREE columns add down the 44 projects to the printed Grand Total $65,377,699.08 / $55,384,182.15 / $9,993,516.93. One project is most of the page: `1 1/14 STM Construct Middle School/High School` is $61,100,887.00 of the $65,377,699.08. AND THE YEARS AGREE ACROSS DOCUMENTS, which is a check neither page can do alone: the 25 projects flagged `fwd` here -- the footer legend reads `fwd - forward from FY 14` and prints no figure -- carry $61,439,547.08 of APPROPRIATED FORWARD between them, and $61,439,547.08 is exactly the BALANCE grand total FY2014's own page 34 prints, read in `fy2014-p34-capital.csv`. Nothing in either document states that identity; it is offered here as corroboration and is not the check that proves this page.

rows.proof: `BOARD OF ASSESSORS`, PDF page 35 of the FY2015 annual town report. READ FROM THE TEXT LAYER, NOT RECOGNISED. The page prints FIVE separate tables and each is footed on its own; column names are read off the printed header (rule 13b.4), and the x band of every figure is given by its right edge, which is constant down each column. TABLE 3, `Fiscal Year 2015 Abstract of Assessments`, twelve property-code classes against the printed TOTALS row. THE ACCOUNTS COLUMN TIES EXACTLY: 5,062, the same count the valuation history prints for FY2015. THE PRINTED VALUATION TOTAL IS THE TOWN'S OWN ERROR AND IS ATTESTED: the twelve rows add to 1,146,501,536, which this page prints TWICE elsewhere -- as the TOTALS of the major-class table and as FY2015's Total Valuation in the history -- while the abstract's own TOTALS cell prints 1,027,856,023, which is exactly the RESIDENTIAL class valuation from the table above it. So the cell carries a figure from the wrong line of the wrong table, by 118,645,513. Read off the born-digital text layer, so this is not a misread: the characters are in the file.

rows.proof: `BOARD OF ASSESSORS`, PDF page 35 of the FY2015 annual town report. READ FROM THE TEXT LAYER, NOT RECOGNISED. The page prints FIVE separate tables and each is footed on its own; column names are read off the printed header (rule 13b.4), and the x band of every figure is given by its right edge, which is constant down each column. TABLE 1, `Fiscal 2015 Assessments and Revenues by Major Property Class`, five classes against the printed TOTALS row. Three columns foot exactly: the levy percentages to 100.0000, the valuations to 1,146,501,536 and the tax levy to 21,003,908.13. The levy is also the valuation at the printed rate -- 1,146,501,536 x 18.32/1000 = 21,003,908.14, a cent out because the rate is per thousand. THE INDUSTRIAL VALUATION IS PRINTED `20,155.100`, with a full stop where the thousands separator belongs; it is recorded here as 20,155,100, which is a PUNCTUATION defect and not a choice of digits -- every digit is present and in order. Two independent identities on this same page fix it: the column then foots to the printed 1,146,501,536 exactly, and the printed Industrial tax levy of 369,241.43 is 20,155,100 x 18.32/1000 to the cent (20,155.10 would give a levy of $369.24). The ABSTRACT table below reaches the same 1,146,501,536 by a different route. ALSO IN THIS FILE, as `line` rows because neither table prints a total: the `Valuation and Tax History`, nine fiscal years, where valuation x rate / 1000 reproduces the printed tax levy within a cent in ALL NINE years and each year's printed Change (%) reproduces the step in the levy; and `New Growth Revenue`, nine fiscal years, where the same arithmetic holds within $1 in SEVEN of the nine -- FY2009 prints 138,168 against 5,077,276 at 12.23 (=62,095) and FY2007 prints 295,074 against 23,809,803 at 12.41 (=295,480). Those two are NOT reconciled and no check here asserts them; the limit is registered as a gap. The FY2015 row of the history repeats the rate, the valuation, the account count and the levy printed in table 1 and the abstract, all four exactly.
